ACK: Acknowledgement: a receiver receipt naming a batch, its file digest, row count and accepted or rejected result.
acknowledged: A batch whose matching receiver acknowledgement confirms acceptance; it does not mean a customer refund was settled.
acknowledgement: The receiver’s durable, identity-checked JSON receipt for one final CSV file.
advisory lock: A named PostgreSQL lock that coordinates workers and is released if its database connection is lost.
API: Application programming interface: the HTTP endpoints through which customers and operations read or submit data.
ASCII: A small character encoding; used here to constrain identifiers and control fields to predictable text.
atomic: Either the whole state change happens or none of it does; other actors do not see a half-finished result.
audit event: A permanent record of a state transition, linked to its chargeback or batch.
backpressure: Bounds on intake or processing that prevent unbounded queues, connections or memory consumption.
batch: A permanent group of chargebacks assigned together to one network, logical partition, slot and CSV file.
bigint: PostgreSQL’s exact signed 64-bit integer type, used for amounts in minor currency units.
boto3: The Python AWS SDK used here to write objects through the S3 protocol.
broker: A message-routing service such as Kafka; Nexo uses PostgreSQL as its work queue instead.
building: Batch membership exists permanently, while CSV generation or manifest commit is unfinished.
CDC: Change data capture: publishing database changes to another system; not implemented in Nexo.
chargeback: A customer’s dispute against an imported card transaction; this system tracks its submission, not settlement.
chunking: Splitting a large workload into bounded groups; Nexo caps each CSV batch’s row count.
claim: Atomically give eligible unassigned chargebacks their one permanent batch membership.
ConfigMap: A Kubernetes object holding non-secret application configuration.
conflict: A terminal batch state indicating evidence disagrees with the recorded identity or file manifest.
connection pool: A bounded set of reusable database connections, avoiding one new connection for every request.
CRLF: Carriage return and line feed: the two-byte line ending used in the CSV contract.
cron: A schedule that runs work at fixed times; Nexo’s slots start four times per UTC day.
CronJob: A Kubernetes object that launches Jobs according to a schedule.
CSV: Comma-separated values: the text file format used for chargeback batches.
cutoff: The six-hour UTC boundary before which a chargeback must have been received to enter a slot.
deduplication: Recognizing an already accepted identity so retrying does not produce a second effect.
Deployment: A Kubernetes object that keeps a chosen number of long-running service pods alive.
digest: A cryptographic fingerprint of exact file bytes; Nexo uses SHA-256.
durable: Committed to persistent storage so a process restart does not erase the result.
exactly-once: One observable effect despite retries; Nexo separately enforces unique membership and reconciles publication, rather than claiming SFTP guarantees it.
export: The process of generating a batch’s one CSV artifact; not a second independent grouping of chargebacks.
file: The deterministic CSV byte sequence and final filename belonging to one batch.
FOR UPDATE: A PostgreSQL row lock that prevents other transactions from changing a selected row before commit.
FTP: File Transfer Protocol: the original requirement’s file-transfer wording; this deployment uses the approved encrypted SFTP protocol.
fsync: Ask the operating system to persist file or directory changes before reporting them durable.
Go: The compiled language used for the HTTP API, authentication and delivery worker.
HSM: Hardware security module: a device that protects sensitive cryptographic keys; outside this learning deployment.
HTTP: Hypertext Transfer Protocol: the request and response protocol used by the API.
HTTPS: HTTP protected by TLS encryption and server authentication.
idempotency: Retrying the same logical operation with the same key produces its original result without a second effect.
idempotency key: A customer-scoped token that identifies one intended chargeback request across retries.
immutable: Once established, the recorded value or identity is not allowed to change.
Job: A Kubernetes object that runs bounded work until completion rather than keeping a service running.
JSON: JavaScript Object Notation: the language-neutral structured format used for API data and acknowledgements.
Kafka: A durable event-streaming broker used in reference designs; not part of Nexo.
kind: Kubernetes in Docker: the local cluster runtime used to exercise the same base manifests as cloud.
Kubernetes: A system that schedules containers and manages service deployments, configuration and scheduled jobs.
ledger: A durable history of financial or processing records; the simulator receipt ledger records identities it has consumed.
manifest: The stored description of a batch artifact: object key, SHA-256, byte count and row count.
minor units: The smallest whole monetary unit represented here; 1250 USD minor units is $12.50.
namespace: A Kubernetes grouping that isolates object names and applies deployment boundaries.
object key: The stable pathname used to identify one file within an object-storage bucket.
object storage: A service that stores byte sequences under keys; accessed using the S3 protocol.
opaque token: A randomly generated credential whose string does not contain trusted identity claims.
PAN: Primary account number: the card number; Nexo never collects or stores it.
partition: One stable logical group used to split row claims within the same PostgreSQL database; default four, configured once for accepted records.
PCI: Payment Card Industry: the ecosystem’s security and compliance rules; no PCI certification is claimed.
pending: A chargeback accepted by the API that has not yet been assigned to a batch.
pgx: The Go PostgreSQL client used for parameterized queries, transactions and connection pooling.
plumbing: Necessary SDK setup or wiring around the core behavior; code labeled this way can be skipped on a first read.
pod: A Kubernetes scheduling unit containing the running container for a workload.
PostgreSQL: The relational database that durably stores Nexo chargebacks, assignments, work state and audit records.
psycopg: The Python PostgreSQL client used by the batch processor and administration tooling.
publication intent: The permanent database flag committed before a temporary upload may be renamed to its final name.
PVC: PersistentVolumeClaim: a Kubernetes request for persistent disk storage.
Python: The language used for CSV batching, the receiver simulator and operational/test tooling.
ready: The batch’s CSV and immutable manifest exist and may be considered for its first publication.
receipt: The simulator’s durable record of a batch result, from which its acknowledgement file is generated.
reconciliation: Comparing durable local intent with receiver evidence to determine what actually happened.
rejected: A matching acknowledgement states that the receiver rejected the batch; it is not reassigned or resubmitted under a new identity.
replica: One running copy of a service; separate replicas coordinate through database state and locks.
retry: Repeat a failed or uncertain operation while preserving its original logical identity and safety rules.
S3: Simple Storage Service: the object-storage protocol used by AWS and compatible providers.
SDK: Software development kit: a real client library used to talk to an external service.
Secret: A Kubernetes object holding credentials populated outside version control.
SFTP: SSH File Transfer Protocol: encrypted file operations over an authenticated SSH connection.
SHA-256: Secure Hash Algorithm, 256-bit: a cryptographic fingerprint used to verify exact request or file bytes.
shard: A physically separate database partition; Nexo’s partitions are logical and physical sharding is not implemented.
SKIP LOCKED: A PostgreSQL option that lets a claimant skip rows another transaction already locked.
slot: One six-hour UTC cutoff and its durable processing record; replaying it does not reset assignments.
SQL: Structured Query Language: the language used to query and enforce relational database state.
SQLite: A small transactional database embedded in the receiver simulator for its separate receipt ledger.
SSH: Secure Shell: the encrypted, authenticated connection underlying SFTP.
StatefulSet: A Kubernetes object for workloads needing stable identity and persistent volumes, used by local infrastructure.
submitted: Matching final file bytes are visible at the receiver, but a matching acceptance acknowledgement is not yet recorded.
synchronous: The caller waits for a response to that call before moving on.
asynchronous: Work begins separately from the initiating event, such as a scheduled Job or a durable work-queue poll.
TLS: Transport Layer Security: encryption and server authentication for HTTPS and database connections.
transaction: Either an imported card purchase, or a database all-or-nothing unit; diagram SQL labels use the database meaning.
TypeScript: The typed source language compiled to JavaScript for the customer UI, operations UI and explorer.
unknown: Publication may have occurred but evidence is missing; Nexo does not republish automatically.
UTC: Coordinated Universal Time: the time standard used for all four daily batch cutoffs.
UTF-8: The Unicode text encoding used for CSV and JSON files.
UUID: Universally unique identifier: the 128-bit identity used for transactions, chargebacks, batches and attempts.
WAL: Write-ahead log: records changes durably before updating stored data; used by PostgreSQL and the simulator’s SQLite.
work queue: Durable pending work claimed by processors; Nexo represents it with indexed PostgreSQL batch state.
ACID: Atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability: the guarantees a relational database transaction provides.
AOF: Append-only file: a persistence log format used by some databases in the references, not a Nexo component.
API gateway: An entry service that routes API traffic and may apply authentication or traffic limits; Nexo uses its API middleware and ingress directly.
AWS: Amazon Web Services: a cloud provider and the origin of the S3 protocol and client libraries.
AZ: Availability zone: an isolated data-center location within one cloud region.
CLI: Command-line interface: commands used to provision synthetic data, run bounded work and operate the system.
CPU: Central processing unit: the processor that executes application instructions.
CVV: Card verification value: the card security code; Nexo never collects it.
DOKS: DigitalOcean Kubernetes: the managed Kubernetes service proposed for the cloud deployment.
EBS: Elastic Block Store: AWS persistent disks, used in cloud cost comparisons.
EKS: Elastic Kubernetes Service: AWS managed Kubernetes, an alternative in the cloud comparison.
exponential backoff: Increasing the delay between failures to reduce pressure on an unavailable dependency; the initial Nexo worker uses a fixed 30-second delay instead.
eventual consistency: Different systems can temporarily disagree while retries or reconciliation bring their states into agreement.
FX: Foreign exchange: converting amounts between currencies; outside Nexo scope.
HA: High availability: redundant resources that keep a system serving through component failures; a single-node learning deployment does not provide it.
HCL: HashiCorp Configuration Language: the declarative syntax used by Terraform infrastructure files.
HMAC: Hash-based message authentication code: a keyed fingerprint used to prove message authenticity.
HTML: Hypertext Markup Language: the structure of the customer, operations and explorer pages.
ID: Identifier: a value that names one record or request without exposing its private contents.
IEEE 754: The standard for binary floating-point numbers; Nexo avoids those numbers for financial amounts.
ISO 4217: The standard that assigns three-letter currency codes such as USD; Nexo uses imported currency codes and does not perform currency conversion.
leader/follower replication: Copying a primary database’s changes to secondary servers; the local one-instance database does not provide this topology.
load balancing: Distributing incoming requests across multiple service replicas.
NAT: Network address translation: routing private machines through an external address; relevant to cloud topology costs.
OLAP: Online analytical processing: large reporting queries over historical data; outside this minimal operational dashboard.
outbox: An event record committed alongside source data so later publication can be retried; the reference pattern is not a separate Nexo service.
p99: The latency at or below which 99 percent of measured requests finish.
PDF: Portable Document Format: the format of the preserved external payment-system references.
PK: Primary key: the database constraint giving every row a unique identity.
PSP: Payment service provider: a generic payment-processing company from the references; Nexo is a chargeback submission system.
PCI-DSS: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard: the card ecosystem’s security controls; Nexo claims no certification.
rate limiting: Limiting how much traffic can arrive over time; Nexo’s current middleware caps concurrent work, not per-customer requests per second.
RDS: Relational Database Service: AWS managed databases, included as a cloud alternative.
request hash: A cryptographic fingerprint of a normalized request used to detect the same idempotency key with different content.
RFC: Request for Comments: the publication series containing many Internet protocol standards.
saga: A multi-step workflow using compensating actions when earlier steps need to be undone; Nexo never undoes permanent batch membership.
SVG: Scalable Vector Graphics: the image format generated from the explorer mapping for linked diagrams.
TPS: Transactions per second: a throughput measure that must be tied to a particular tested operation and environment.
TTL: Time to live: how long a record or key is retained; Nexo does not expire accepted idempotency identities or batch membership.
UI: User interface: the pages through which a customer or operator exercises the real API.
VM: Virtual machine: a cloud compute instance that can run a Kubernetes node.
VS Code: Visual Studio Code: the editor opened by source links generated from the actual symbol location.
XA: A standard interface for coordinating distributed database transactions; it does not make SFTP transactional.
2PC: Two-phase commit: a protocol for coordinating all-or-nothing changes across participants; not provided by SFTP.
RPO: Recovery point objective: the maximum acceptable amount of committed history lost after a failure.
RTO: Recovery time objective: the maximum acceptable time to restore service after a failure.
p50: The median latency: half of measured requests finish at or below this time.
p95: The latency at or below which 95 percent of measured requests finish.
RSS: Resident set size: the operating-system memory currently held in physical memory by a process.
tracemalloc: Python tooling that measures allocations made through its memory allocator; it adds measurement overhead.
cgroup: A Linux operating-system mechanism that limits and accounts for a group of processes, including containers.
vCPU: Virtual CPU: a share of processing capacity assigned to a virtual machine.
GiB: Gibibyte: 1,073,741,824 bytes, a unit used for memory and storage capacity.
MiB: Mebibyte: 1,048,576 bytes, a unit used for memory and file sizes.
millicore: One thousandth of a CPU; Kubernetes uses this unit for resource requests and limits.
loopback: A network address that connects back to the same computer instead of exposing a service externally.
